Make the HTML the demonstration.

The biggest opportunity is to let visitors see a small website take shape. ItsyWeb’s current home page spends its strongest visual space on a terminal walkthrough. The new page should show what the tool makes possible before explaining the operational steps.

What the framework sites get right

A stronger home-page story

My recommendation is a demonstration-led page with more expressive typography, a shorter opening and a distinct purpose for each section. Keep the approved logo and navy/ice identity as the starting constraints.

  1. Introduce HTML with the useful extras included.

    Lead with the positive offer. Put “Build your first site” beside a compact install command. Keep the operating-system requirements visible near installation.

  2. Show a page, a layout and their rendered result.

    Use the bookshop from Getting Started so the home page and tutorial feel connected. A small switcher can demonstrate a shared header and a clean URL. On mobile, stack code and result; avoid a miniature desktop editor.

  3. Show how the site can grow.

    Briefly demonstrate optional on-page editing, then link to Contact and Blog. These capabilities are documented but absent from the current home-page story. Keep them secondary to ordinary HTML.

  4. Explain local development and ownership.

    Show the path from files to local preview to a server the visitor controls. Put setup, SSH deployment, automatic HTTPS, branch destinations and recovery here, with the Ubuntu, domain and network prerequisites intact.

  5. Make the next step small and clear.

    Close with the working bookshop tutorial and installation details. Consolidate the current repeated command walkthroughs so each section adds information.

Draft opening message

Proposed wording for discussion. This shifts emphasis from avoiding a build pipeline to what the visitor can make.

Your HTML.
A working website.

Write HTML and CSS with shared layouts, partials and clean URLs. ItsyWeb gives you local preview and a way to publish to your own server, with automatic HTTPS.

Build your first site

What changes visually

Give the headline and demonstration room to lead. Use a distinctive display face with a quiet reading face, precise code labels and fewer competing text sizes. Explore a light opening with a navy code pane, then a darker server-and-deployment section. Reserve ice blue for emphasis and visible changes in the demo.

Use one purposeful interaction: changing a shared template updates the sample page. Let lower sections alternate between demonstrations, concise explanation and a workflow diagram. This gives the page rhythm without turning every capability into the same card.

How the docs should match

Carry over the header, logo, heading family, link color, code-pane treatment and focus states. Preserve the docs’ reading measure, sidebar, tutorial order and mobile navigation. A matching type and token pass should be enough initially.

Both Svelte’s docs and Nuxt’s docs keep their identity recognizable while giving reading and navigation a conventional layout.

Inspection scope and limits

Reviewed November 14, 2026: the live ItsyWeb home page on desktop and at a 390px mobile viewport; the current checkout’s home-page content and shared CSS; all four framework home pages at 1280px, including representative lower sections; Nuxt’s Routing demo interaction; and the Svelte, Nuxt and ItsyWeb docs openings. Screenshots above are reference captures, not proposed ItsyWeb designs. Mobile framework layouts, full accessibility and performance were not audited. Recommendations are design judgments, not measured conversion results.

Research and a proposed content baseline only. Visual direction remains open; the next design step is a comparable set of home-page concepts using this story. No production templates, styles or deployment settings have changed.
